editorial:
Imagine sitting down for a family dinner where everyone is trying to be polite, but there is a lot of tension hiding under the surface. You follow the Apple family in Rhinebeck, New York, on a chilly election night in 2010. The kids have all gathered to surprise their Uncle Benjamin with a new dog since his old one passed away. It feels like a cozy home movie at first, but as the night goes on, the conversation shifts from simple memories to heated debates about politics and how they all view the world. It is a quiet, character-driven story that feels like you are eavesdropping on a real family gathering.

What really makes this work is how the actors handle the dialogue. The pacing is slow, so if you love big explosions or fast plots, this might not be for you. However, if you enjoy watching people talk and clash, you will love the chemistry here. The pros are the realistic acting and the cozy setting, while the con is that it takes a while to get moving. You should definitely check this out if you like smart dramas.
endingExplained: As the night ends and the election results come in, the family has to face the reality of their different beliefs. The tension peaks during the dinner, but the arrival of the new puppy helps soften the mood. Instead of a huge explosion, the movie wraps up with a feeling of acceptance. You see that while they will never agree on politics, the love for their uncle and their family bond is more important than any vote.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character studies and realistic family arguments.
